title: Design a distributed rate limiter
statement:
Your company exposes a public REST API served by 40 stateless API servers behind a load balancer. Design the rate limiter that enforces limits such as "100 requests per minute per API key" and "10 login attempts per hour per IP address" across all servers. A client that exceeds a limit gets HTTP 429 with a hint about when to retry.

Clarify or state any other requirements and assumptions you need, then walk through your design.
facts: 1 million active API keys; peak traffic is 200,000 requests per second.
The rate limiter may add at most 5 ms to a request at the 99th percentile.
Limits differ by plan (free, pro, enterprise) and the product team changes them without a deployment.

keyPoints.text: chooses and explains an algorithm (token bucket, sliding window log or counter, fixed window) and its accuracy at window boundaries
keeps the counters in a shared low-latency store such as Redis, so every API server sees the same counts
makes check-and-increment atomic (an atomic increment with expiry, or a script run on the store) so two servers cannot both let a request through over the limit
decides what happens when the counter store is unavailable, failing open or closed per limit, and says why
returns 429 with Retry-After and rate-limit headers so clients can back off
partitions counters by key across a store cluster and keeps hot keys from overloading one node
loads the limit rules from a configuration store and caches them on each server with a short refresh
reduces round trips at 200,000 requests per second, for example with a local pre-check, batching or a sidecar

probes.FAILURE_HANDLING: The Redis cluster holding the counters becomes unreachable for two minutes. What does your API do during that time?
probes.SCALABILITY: Traffic grows to 2 million requests per second. What changes in your design?
probes.RELIABILITY: Two API servers check the same key at the same moment. How do you make sure the limit is not exceeded?
probes.TRADE_OFFS: Why that algorithm? What does it get wrong at window boundaries, and when would you pick another one?
probes.API_DESIGN: What does a client see when it is throttled, and how does it know when to retry?
probes.OBSERVABILITY: How would you find out that the rate limiter is wrongly blocking legitimate customers?
